faq.q: How does an arch dam work?
faq.a: An arch dam curves upstream. Water pressure squeezes the curve, and the arch passes the force sideways into the canyon walls, just as an arch bridge passes load into its abutments.

faq.q: How does a gravity dam work?
faq.a: A gravity dam is a massive wedge of concrete or masonry. Its weight presses it onto the rock, creating enough friction to stop the water sliding it away or tipping it over.

faq.q: Why does an arch dam curve toward the water?
faq.a: With the curve bulging upstream, water pressure squeezes the arch, putting the concrete in compression, which it handles very well. Curved the other way, the water would try to pull it apart.
asks: Which way does an arch dam curve?

faq.q: Where can arch dams be built?
faq.a: In narrow canyons with strong, solid rock on both sides, because the walls must take the arch's huge sideways thrust. Weak or wide valleys need gravity or embankment dams.
asks: Why aren't all dams arch dams?

faq.q: What kind of dam is the Hoover Dam?
faq.a: The Hoover Dam is an arch-gravity dam: it curves upstream like an arch and is also very thick and heavy, so it uses both its shape and its weight to hold back Lake Mead.
asks: Is the Hoover Dam an arch dam?

facts: The Hoover Dam on the Colorado River, completed in 1936, is a concrete arch-gravity dam 221 metres high.
An arch dam can use far less concrete than a gravity dam of the same height, because the canyon walls carry much of the load.

quiz.say: An engineer must dam a wide valley with weak, crumbly sides. Which type is the better choice?
quiz.show: Wide valley, weak sides. Better dam?
quiz.why: A gravity dam relies on its own weight rather than the valley sides, so weak sides matter less.

wrong.1: An arch dam needs strong rock sides to take its sideways thrust.
wrong.2: Gravity and embankment dams are built across wide valleys all the time.
